## Two competing accounts and distinction

H1: a reported difference is only an inconsistent transport of units, loss or constraints and disappears when corresponding optimization problems are exactly matched. H2: an explicitly identified restriction of the shared model family or penalty remains different after proper transport, so it defines a real inductive constraint rather than a new coordinate-only benefit. These accounts concern different controlled configurations, not two equally plausible answers to the exact identity in F1.

Comparison: first define g_theta(j,I)=max(0,mu_j+s_j*f_theta(j,I)), and use identical data/parameter indexing, transported loss and the same penalty on corresponding theta. Compare argmin sets and pointwise actions, allowing nonunique minimizers. Then change only a specified family/penalty closure condition, derive whether a separating constructed instance exists. A risk difference between arbitrarily selected minimizers does not alone disprove optimization-problem equivalence. No generated performance score is needed.
